spatial_claims.claim: C is a point on segment AB (between A and B)
C lies on AB with AC greater than CB (C divides AB with the longer part toward A)
The rectangle AB * CB equals the square on AC (area relationship from Prop 2.11)
AB, AC, CB are three straight lines in proportion: AB : AC = AC : CB

configuration_map: Point C lies on segment AB, between A and B, positioned such that AC > CB (i.e., C is closer to B than to A). This is the standard golden ratio division point. The configuration is a single line segment with one interior point — no angles, triangles, circles, or complex figures are involved. All reasoning after the construction is purely proportional.
pass_reason: The proof makes only minimal spatial claims: a single point C on segment AB with AC > CB. These claims are trivially consistent with each other and remain so throughout the proof. The rest of the argument is purely algebraic/proportional (applying Prop 2.11 for construction and the converse of Prop 6.17 for the proportion). No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no ray orderings — nothing that could generate a spatial contradiction.
